scope: Opinion-read latency while a generative adjudication runs, before and after the interleaving worker (reads served at the generation's pauses). benchmarks/lfm25/interleave_latency.py against one daemon at a time, baseline and interleave alternating, two rounds of n=20 per binary. Reads are full misses (distinct inputs). Latencies are client wall-clock ms over HTTP on localhost.
workload: generation: 309-token single-line email, 94.5 completion tokens p50 (a schema report), ~1.4 s wall alone; read: 13-token email, questions [verdict], ~0.55 s of work (prefill + describe + score)
conditions: Shared GPU: the live lfm2d-system1 pod (mostly idle) and a kaiseki torch process holding 68 GB were resident in every round; a candle-batch decode benchmark ran during an earlier pair of rounds (not these; those are not reported). Rounds alternate binaries so drift lands on both.
reading: A read fired during a generation waited for the rest of it before (queue p50 573/804 ms, p90 843/990); now it waits for the generation's next pause (queue p50 9 ms, max 153/175 ms, about one 128-token prefill chunk; a decode pause is one token, ~10 ms). The generation grows by about the read's own work (added beyond it: p50 -46/+20 ms, p90 +10/+299 ms), and its text and token count match its alone run in every pair (asserted). Baseline's generation_with_read is not comparable to its alone column: there the read ran after the generation, outside its wall time. baseline-r1's generation_alone includes slow outliers (max 4778 ms) the other rounds do not.
